draft.title: GST and price
card: GST is the goods and services tax. In Australia it is 10% of the price before tax. It is added to the price of most goods and services.
Adding GST
price with GST = price without GST × 1.1. Example: a $200 bike has GST of $20, so it costs $200 × 1.1 = $220.
Removing GST
price without GST = price with GST ÷ 1.1. The GST is the 10% of the price without GST, not 10% of the total.
Example
A jacket costs $330 with GST. Without GST it is $330 ÷ 1.1 = $300. The GST is $330 − $300 = $30.
draft.remember: Times 1.1 to add GST. Divide by 1.1 to take it off.

a.q: A printer costs $450 before GST. What is its price including GST?
a.why: Price with GST = $450 × 1.1 = $495. Subtracting 10% gives $405, which takes GST off instead of adding it.
a.clue: Adding GST means multiplying the price before GST.

b.q: Mia buys a desk for $1100 including GST. How much of that price is GST?
b.why: Price without GST = $1100 ÷ 1.1 = $1000, so the GST is $1100 − $1000 = $100. Taking 10% of $1100 gives $110, but GST is 10% of the price before GST, not of the total.
b.clue: Find the price without GST first, then subtract.

problems.detail: Why (a) says subtracting 10% to get $405 'takes GST off'. That is not how GST is removed: the card says to divide by 1.1, which would give $409.09. The why should say $405 is simply wrong, so students do not learn that taking 10% off removes GST.
'The GST is the 10% of the price without GST' has a stray 'the' and reads awkwardly. It should read 'GST is 10% of the price without GST'.

check.summary: Both questions are correct, with answers $495 and $100. Why (a) wrongly implies that subtracting 10% removes GST, which contradicts the card's divide-by-1.1 method, and there is a small grammar slip on the card.
